title: Line Charges, Coupon and Certificate Allocation on Tailwise Online and In-Store Orders
content:
Each line of a Tailwise Online and In-Store Orders purchase is charged on its own: quantity times unit price, with at most the method's largest quantity of one item per line.

### Charging clause

1. At most the method's number of promotional coupons apply to an order.
2. An order-level coupon is allocated over the lines by the method's coupon allocation basis (pro rata by line subtotal).
3. Certificates, where the method accepts Pals Rewards certificates, are allocated by the method's certificate allocation basis after coupons, and never on excluded categories.
4. The line amount billed is quantity times unit price, less the coupon allocated to the line and less the certificate allocated to it, rounded half up to the cent; a rounding cent goes to the highest line.
5. A substitution, where the method allows substitution and the customer allowed substitutions, is charged by the method's substitute price rule (the lower of the original and the substitute).

### Worked example (hypothetical order)

| Line | Quantity times unit price | Coupon allocated (of a $10.00 coupon) | Certificate allocated (of a $5.00 certificate) | Line amount billed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Line 1 | 2 units at $18.00, $36.00 | $6.00 | $3.00 | $27.00 |
| Line 2 | 1 unit at $24.00, $24.00 | $4.00 | $2.00 | $18.00 |

The line subtotals are $36.00 and $24.00, so each line takes 60% and 40% of the coupon by line subtotal; the certificate is spread the same way after the coupon. Line 1 is $36.00 less $6.00 less $3.00, which is $27.00.

### Points of judgement

- The coupon and the certificate are each taken off the line's own quantity times unit price; neither is applied to a fee.
- A method that does not accept certificates allocates none to its lines.
- A substitute for a hypothetical $12.99 item priced $13.49 is charged $12.99, the lower of the two.
